Author: Martin Tepel, Markus van der Giet, Mario Statz, Joachim Jankowski and Walter Zidek
Comment: The eligible cardiovascular mortality outcome is a secondary endpoint. The primary composite cardiovascular endpoint and all-cause mortality were intentionally excluded. Title: Effects of vitamin E on cardiovascular outcomes in people with mild-to-moderate renal insufficiency: Results of the HOPE Study
Author: Mann et al.
Comment: The paper is a post-hoc analysis of the renal-insufficiency subgroup of the larger HOPE randomized trial. Table 2 explicitly labels the estimate as RR; the event-count risk ratio calculated directly from 57/499 versus 57/494 is close but not identical, likely because the reported estimate comes from the paper's stratified time-to-event analysis. Both the verbatim counts and the paper-reported RR are retained.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Natural-source vitamin E (RRR-alpha-tocopheryl acetate), 400 IU once daily') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Post-hoc CKD-subgroup analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled 2×2 factorial trial
domain: Chronic kidney disease and cardiovascular mortality
Study Environment: Multicenter clinical trial conducted at 267 participating centers
Country: 19 countries in North and South America and Europe
Content length: 400 IU once daily for an average/median follow-up of 4.5 years
Topic of Content: Antioxidant therapy and cardiovascular outcomes in mild-to-moderate renal insufficiency

effect_direction: little to no difference; numerically lower cardiovascular mortality with antioxidant therapy

Title: Bardoxolone Methyl in Type 2 Diabetes and Stage 4 Chronic Kidney Disease
Author: de Zeeuw et al.
Comment: The paper defines cardiovascular death as death due to either cardiovascular or unknown causes. Counts of 27/1088 and 19/1097 are the whole-follow-up cardiovascular-death component and are suitable for calculating the review's risk ratio. The paper reports a hazard ratio, not a risk ratio; no RR was entered. Do not use the secondary-composite first-event cardiovascular-death counts (19 vs 13) or all-cause death counts (44 vs 31). Median follow-up was 9 months, and the trial was terminated early.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Bardoxolone methyl 20 mg once daily plus background conventional therapy') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: Phase 3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial
Country: United States, European Union, Australia, Canada, Israel, and Mexico
Medium: Oral bardoxolone methyl 20 mg once daily
Participant type: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and stage 4 chronic kidney disease
Outcome measurement: Death from cardiovascular causes, defined by the trial as death due to either cardiovascular or unknown causes and evaluated by an independent events-adjudication committee
effect_direction: higher cardiovascular mortality with antioxidant or Nrf2-activating therapy
